chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says, after Friday, when he departs sitting down before bowing [in the two rak'ahs of Fajr or the sunnah], Al-Hamd [Al-Fatiha] once, and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' seven times, and 'Qul A'udhu bi Rabb al-Falaq' seven times, and 'Qul A'udhu bi Rabb al-Nas' seven times, and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), and the Verse of Humiliation (Ayat al-Sukhrah), and the end of His saying 'Hasana Rasoolun min anfusikum' until its end, it will be an expiation for what is between one Friday and the next.
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: Then stand up and establish [prayer] for Asr, up to his saying, and know that the narration has come.

key_terms.آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
key_terms.قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ اَلنّاسِ: Qul A'udhu bi Rabb al-Nas (Surah An-Nas)
key_terms.قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ اَلْفَلَقِ: Qul A'udhu bi Rabb al-Falaq (Surah Al-Falaq)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dhikr to recite after Friday prayer for expiation of sins?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific post-Friday prayer dhikr routine, emphasizing the recitation of Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and al-Nas alongside key verses like Ayat al-Kursi. This practice is highlighted in Shia jurisprudence as a means of spiritual purification, with the promise that it serves as an expiation (kaffarah) for minor sins committed between the current and next Friday, reinforcing the sanctity of the day.
